blocks.text: **Tilde makes everyday things you can tap or scan.** Hold your phone to one, or point its camera at the code, and your phone does something useful: it saves a contact, joins the Wi-Fi, opens a link, books a meeting. You print them yourself, then choose what each one opens with the Tilde app.

items.text: **Cards:** the Tilde Card, a business card with a QR code on the front and an NFC sticker inside.
**Fobs:** coins and tags for your keys, in Base and Premium, and the Special Edition: Retro handheld.
**Home & desk:** the sticky note and the grocery list for the fridge, the Wi-Fi coaster, the calendar, the Tilde Stand and the Stand Mini.
**The app:** Tilde for Android, which writes what each one opens, and puts your card on your phone.

blocks.text: **Print a few, tag everything.** Any phone reads them; the app writes them. Tilde is Android only for now, and your iPhone reads every tag.

items.text: **Scan:** any phone’s camera reads a printed code. No app needed.
**Tap:** an NFC sticker sits inside, under the tap icon. Hold the back of the phone flat on the icon, within 1–2 cm.
sub: **iPhone XS or newer:** reads a tap with the screen on, with no app and no setting. A link comes up as a notification. Not while Camera or Wallet is open.
**iPhone 7 to X:** open the NFC reader in Control Center first.
**Android:** NFC must be on, and the phone unlocked. A link opens. A contact card offers to save it. Guest Wi-Fi offers Connect.

items.text: **Write:** the sticker can be rewritten any time, through the plastic.
sub: **Android:** Tilde for Android’s **Write a sticker**. It writes a link, your contact card, or your guest Wi-Fi. Notes and lists are coming in the next app update.
**iPhone:** Tilde is Android only for now. To write a link from an iPhone, use the free NFC Tools app.

items.text: **What an iPhone does with a tap:**
sub: **A contact card:** if iPhone users will tap it, write a link instead (your website or a contact page): iPhones open links from a tap. To save your contact, an iPhone scans your phone’s code.
**Guest Wi-Fi:** an iPhone joins by scanning the Wi-Fi code.
**A note or a list** (coming in the next app update): a tap opens the note page, with no app.

items.text: **Which sticker:** a round NFC sticker, 25 mm. An NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link or your guest Wi-Fi. Search “NTAG216 25mm round NFC sticker”.
**Anything on a sticker or a printed code is public:** anyone who taps or scans it can read it. Write only what you’d put on a poster.

blocks.text: **Tilde for Android:** download the APK from its GitHub releases page, with the install steps (Android 8.0 or newer). It’s free, open source (MIT) and needs no account.

items.text: **Get the files:** every model is free on GitHub, at [github.com/tbutman/tilde-card](https://github.com/tbutman/tilde-card): MIT in the repo, CC BY 4.0 on MakerWorld. Open a model in **OpenSCAD’s Customizer**, type your settings (your link, your colors, your icon), export it, and print it with the steps in [PRINTING.md](https://github.com/tbutman/tilde-card/blob/main/PRINTING.md).

**In color:** export a **3MF**, not an STL: the colors are flush inlays, and an STL merges them into one plain piece. A recent OpenSCAD development snapshot keeps the colors in the 3MF; open it in Bambu Studio and choose the process again.

**MakerWorld’s Model Maker** is the same customizer in your browser: you change the settings and download a 3MF that’s ready to print. The Tilde listings on MakerWorld aren’t public yet; when they are, each product links its listing here.

**You’ll need** a 3D printer (a multi-color one, such as a Bambu Lab printer with an AMS, for anything in more than one color), PLA, and round NFC stickers. Each product’s **What you need** lists the rest.

**Printable now:** the Tilde Card, the fobs, the Retro handheld (Base), the sticky note, the grocery list, the calendar, the Wi-Fi coaster and the Tilde Stand. **Coming soon:** the Stand Mini’s files, and the Premium handheld. Writing notes and lists from the app comes in the next app update.

oneLiner.text: a business card you print yourself, with your QR code on the front and an NFC sticker sealed inside.

problem.text: paper cards get lost and go stale. This one opens your link from a scan or a tap, and the sticker can be rewritten when your link changes.

items: **Scan:** the code on the front opens your link.
**Tap:** the NFC sticker sits behind the tap waves, in the strip beside the code. Hold the phone there, within 1–3 cm. It reads from either side.
**One solid piece:** the printer pauses so you can drop the sticker in, then prints over it, in a single print.
**Save my contact:** hand it over; they scan or tap.
**A link:** your portfolio, LinkedIn or booking page.
**WhatsApp:** a tap opens a chat with you.
**The fobs:** the same uses on your keys: a Base tag or a Premium coin in the card’s colors.
**Tilde Card, Two-Piece:** the same designs, with a back you can swap.
**7 fronts:** Classic, Minimal, Mystery, Handle, Badge, Tap only, Blank.
**Code and text:** QR size (Small, Medium, Full), your name, handle, link (up to 53 characters), website, role.
**5 backs:** a terminal window, Plain, Contact, Code, or none.
**Marks:** a mark over the sticker (a ring, the tap waves, or both), and the tap mark on the back.
**Colors:** 7 themes (Dark, Light, Signal, Portugal, Brasil, USA, Retro), or your own palette.
**Your own logo:** there’s no logo setting. Choose the plain back (Back: None) and add your text or logo in Bambu Studio, on the back’s top face (PRINTING.md, “Make it yours”).

specs.text: credit-card size, 85.60 × 53.98 mm; 1.8 mm thick with a thin sticker, 2.0 with a thick one. PLA, up to 4 colors.

items: **NFC sticker:** 1 round sticker, 22–25 mm, thin: an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link. Search “NTAG216 25mm round NFC sticker”.
**Printer:** multi-color (AMS or similar) for the card’s colors; a 0.4 mm nozzle (0.2 for finer text).
**The pause:** add one pause in Bambu Studio at the sticker’s layer (PRINTING.md says which).
**Print time:** about 1 h on a 0.4 mm nozzle, at the default settings; about 17.5 g of PLA.
**Difficulty:** medium (one pause to time).

**Save my contact.**
**A link.**
**One card, many looks:** swap the back for an event.
**A tap card for your wallet:** a blank front and no back print, in a wallet’s outside pocket.
**The fobs:** the same uses on your keys: a Base tag or a Premium coin in the card’s colors.
**Tilde Card, Solid:** for a card that’s sealed for good.

specs.text: 85.60 × 53.98 mm; 1.8 mm thick with a thin sticker, 2.0 with a thick one; the back piece is 0.8 mm. PLA, up to 4 colors, all in the first 3 layers.

items: **NFC sticker:** 1 round sticker, 22–25 mm, thin: an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link. Search “NTAG216 25mm round NFC sticker”.

oneLiner.text: a thin tag for your keys, with a QR code on the front and an NFC sticker inside.

problem.text: the thing you keep looking up (a tracking page, a booking, your Wi-Fi), on your keyring, a scan or a tap away.

items: **Scan:** the code opens its link.
**Tap:** the sticker sits under the code.
**No glue needed:** the back piece presses in past a lip, and the key ring through both pieces holds it shut, so the sticker can be swapped. Glue it for the most durable tag.
**A link (a physical bookmark):** several tags flip on one ring like index cards.
**Return my lost keys:** a link that reaches you, such as a WhatsApp chat.
**Book a meeting:** your booking link.
**WhatsApp:** a chat with you, from a tap or a scan.
**Base coin:** tap only, for the same ring.
**Tilde Card:** the same theme in your wallet.
**Retro handheld:** a tag with a different shape.
**The link:** up to 53 characters (the tag grows with it); the ring hole through both pieces or the front only.
**Earless:** no tab or ring hole.
**Colors:** the card’s 7 themes, or your own.
**Icon:** 37 generic icons, the tap waves, inlaid or engraved, and a short label.

specs.text: 28.8 × 35.3 mm (links up to 17 characters), 31 × 37.5 (up to 32), 35 × 41.5 (up to 53); 1.8 mm thick. PLA, about 5.7 g.

items: **NFC sticker:** 1 round sticker, 22–25 mm across (25.5 at most), 0.10–0.20 mm thick (thicker up to 0.40 mm: set NFC Sticker to Thick): an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link. Search “NTAG216 25mm round NFC sticker”.
**Printer:** multi-color (an AMS or similar), for the inlaid code and icon; one color for an engraved tag.
**Filament:** PLA, 3 colors, about 5.7 g (black 3.0, white 1.7, orange 0.9 at the defaults).
**Print time:** about 29 min alone on an A1 mini (less when several share a plate).
**A split key ring:** it holds the back in, no glue needed. The earless tag has no hole: glue its back piece.
**Difficulty:** easy: press the back in, put the ring on.

oneLiner.text: a small round fob for your keys, tap only, with an icon on its face.

problem.text: one tap shares or opens something, with no code to print and nothing to type.

items: **Tap** the face: the sticker is inside, behind the icon. There’s no code.

**Open and close by hand:** the back twists in with a quarter turn and locks. Open it with a firm twist the other way, to swap the sticker. You rarely need to: a phone rewrites it through the plastic.
**A second hold:** the key ring through both halves of the tab stops it turning.
**Return my lost keys:** a house icon on your house keys, opening a chat with you.
**Guest Wi-Fi:** Android guests tap; iPhones scan a Wi-Fi code.
**Save my contact:** your link or contact card on your keychain.
**WhatsApp:** a chat with you.
**Base tag:** add a code to scan.
**Premium coin:** the same job, heavier, locked with a key.
**Tilde Card:** the same colors.
**Tightness:** five settings, from easiest to tightest (snug by default).
**Coin slot:** off by default; with it, a US quarter or a 20 euro cent opens the back.
**A mark on the back:** none, Tilde’s `~/`, or your own short label.
**Edges:** round or sharp. **Earless:** no tab or ring hole.
**Colors and icon:** as the tag.

specs.text: 32 × 41.5 mm with its tab, 3.4 mm thick; earless, 32 × 32 mm. PLA, about 5.6 g.

items: **NFC sticker:** 1 round sticker, 22–25 mm across (25.5 at most), 0.10–0.20 mm thick (thicker up to 0.40 mm: set NFC Sticker to Thick): an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link. Search “NTAG216 25mm round NFC sticker”.
**Printer:** multi-color for an inlaid icon; one color for an engraved one.
**Filament:** PLA, 2 colors, about 5.6 g (black 4.1, orange 1.5).
**Print time:** about 22 min alone.
**A split key ring** (none for the earless coin). No glue: the back twists on.
**Difficulty:** easy: the quickest; drop the back in and give it a quarter turn.

problem.text: a tag that lasts on keys and doesn’t come open in a pocket.

items: **Scan** the front; **tap** the sticker inside.
**The lock:** the back sits flush, your icon fills it, and it locks with a quarter turn of the T-key, a small printed key. It can’t be opened or closed by hand. One T-key opens every Premium fob.
**A link (a physical bookmark).**
**Book a meeting.**
**Save my contact.**

**The T-key:** prints with it.
**Premium coin:** the same series, tap only.

**Premium tightness:** four settings (the default closes easily with the T-key).
**T-key:** print one with it, or leave it off (one key opens them all).

**The link, colors and icon:** as the Base tag.

specs.text: 36 × 44 mm (links up to 32 characters), 37 × 44.5 (up to 53); earless, 36 × 36. About 6 mm thick. PLA, 4 walls; about 14.8 g with its T-key.

items: **NFC sticker:** 1 round sticker, 22–25 mm across (25.5 at most), 0.10–0.20 mm thick (thicker up to 0.40 mm: set NFC Sticker to Thick): an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link. Search “NTAG216 25mm round NFC sticker”.
**Printer:** multi-color; set 4 wall loops.

**Print time:** about 46 min alone, with its T-key (the key adds about 7.5 min and 4.5 g; leave it off if you have one).
**A split key ring.** No glue: the T-key locks it.
**Difficulty:** medium: longer, 4 walls, and it closes only with the printed T-key.

oneLiner.text: a tag shaped like a classic handheld game console: a screen, a D-pad and buttons, in color.

problem.text: a fob people want to pick up, so the tap or scan behind it gets tried.

items: **Base:** the QR code is on the back and the sticker inside. Scan or tap.
**Premium:** your icon is on the back, so it’s tap only, and it locks with the T-key like every Premium fob.
A generic console: no brand names or logos.
**A link (a physical bookmark):** a playlist, a game, your portfolio.
**Save my contact:** a conversation starter on a bag or a lanyard.
**A gift:** a link to a message or a photo album.
**Base tag:** the everyday version.
**Premium coin:** the same lock and key.
**Size:** Large (the console’s proportions) or Standard (the tag’s size).
**Colors:** Light or Dark.
**Screen:** blank, or a pixel `~/` in three styles.
**Back:** the QR code (Base), or an icon and label; its details engraved, printed or none.
**Ring hole:** an eyelet at the top, through the corner, or none (earless).
**Premium:** the controls recessed, flush or raised (glued-in pieces), and the speaker slots grooved or flush.
**Base:** Large 31 × 47.8 mm (35 × 54 for longer links), 1.8 mm thick; Standard, the Base tag’s size.
**Premium:** Large 36 × 63.5 mm with the eyelet (36 × 55.5 without), Standard 36 × 44; about 6 mm thick.
PLA in off-white, near-black, olive (the screen) and wine (the buttons).

**NFC sticker:** 1 round sticker, 22–25 mm across (25.5 at most), 0.10–0.20 mm thick (thicker up to 0.40 mm: set NFC Sticker to Thick): an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link. Search “NTAG216 25mm round NFC sticker”.
**Printer:** multi-color, 4 colors. You set the first layer’s color order by hand (the model’s notes say how).
**Filament:** PLA, 4 colors: off-white, near-black, olive and wine (matte recommended).
**Base:** about 7.5 g Large, 6.8 g Standard.
**Premium:** about 20.8 g Large, 18.1 g Standard, with its T-key.
**Print time:** about 38 min Base Large, 37 min Base Standard; about 65 min Premium Large, 60 min Premium Standard.
**Glue:** none, except gel superglue for Premium’s raised controls (wipe with isopropyl alcohol first).
**Difficulty:** medium; raised controls are advanced (small glued pieces).

oneLiner.text: a printed sticky note for the fridge or the desk, with a tap icon and an NFC sticker inside.

problem.text: the note you’d leave for the family (the Wi-Fi, who to call, when you’re back) as a tap you update from your phone, not a scrawl you rewrite.

items: **Tap** the tap icon: the sticker is under it.
**Today:** it opens whatever you write to it, like any sticker: a link, your contact card, your guest Wi-Fi.

**Coming in the next app update, notes:** write a note in Tilde (“Back at 6, dinner’s in the fridge”), then Write a sticker. A tap opens the note on a page, on any phone, with no app. To change it, edit it in Tilde and tap the sticker again.
**Anyone who taps it can read it.**
**On the fridge:** magnets in the back. On a desk: the cradle, or the thin back.
**Guest Wi-Fi on the fridge:** Android guests tap; iPhones scan a Wi-Fi code.
**A note for the family:** for the sitter or the kids (coming in the next app update).
**Save my contact:** the family’s numbers, as a contact card.
**A link:** the school calendar, the takeout menu.
**Grocery list:** the same back, for the list.
**Calendar:** the same family on the fridge.
**Wi-Fi coaster:** guest Wi-Fi with a code iPhones can scan.
**Size:** large (76 mm) or small (51 mm).
**The tap icon:** on or off, in a corner or the center.
**The back:** thin (no magnets), thick solid, or thick and light.
**Magnets:** outside, inside, or off. A pry cutaway to lift it, and a folded corner.
**A cradle** for the desk.
**Colors:** yellow and black, or your own.

specs.text: 76 × 76 mm (small 51 × 51); the face is 1.6 mm, a thick back 5 mm. PLA, about 21 g (thin back) to 36 g (thick solid).

items: **NFC sticker:** 1 round 25 mm sticker (an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link); an **anti-metal** one (25 × 1.0 mm, ferrite side down) for the thick backs on a fridge.

oneLiner.text: a printed list for the fridge, handwritten-style (“milk, bread, eggs”), with an NFC sticker inside.

problem.text: the list on the fridge is never the one in your pocket.

items: **Today:** a tap opens whatever you write to the sticker, such as a link. Tilde doesn’t make lists yet.

**Coming in the next app update, lists:** make the list in Tilde, then Write a sticker. A tap opens the list on a page with tick boxes, on any phone, with no app. Your ticks stay on your phone; they don’t change the list on the fridge. To update it, edit it in Tilde and tap the sticker again.
**It doesn’t sync:** the list on the page is what’s on the sticker. Only its owner updates it, in Tilde.
**Anyone who taps it can read the list.**
**The shopping list on the fridge:** tap it on the way out, and the list is on your phone (coming in the next app update).
**The week’s meal plan,** the same way (coming in the next app update).
**Sticky note:** the same back and magnets.
**Calendar:** the family’s fridge.
**Size:** tall (76 × 102 mm) or short (76 × 76).
**The print:** a title and up to six items, each open, ticked or struck; the tap row’s words and layout.
**The back, magnets, cradle and colors:** as the sticky note (white, navy and khaki by default).

specs.text: 76 × 102 mm (short 76 × 76); the face is 1.6 mm. PLA, about 28 g (tall).

items: **NFC sticker:** 1 round 25 mm sticker, under the tap doodle (an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link); anti-metal for the thick backs on a fridge.

oneLiner.text: a weighted coaster with your Wi-Fi’s QR code and network name on top, and an NFC sticker under the Wi-Fi icon.

problem.text: “What’s the Wi-Fi?”, answered without reading out a password.

items: **Scan:** the printed Wi-Fi code joins the network, on iPhones and Android phones.
**Tap** the Wi-Fi icon: an Android phone offers Connect. iPhones scan the code.
**A new password:** rewrite the sticker with the app; the printed code needs a new top.
**Guest Wi-Fi at home:** on the coffee table.
**A café or a shared office:** the code at every table (with the owner’s OK).
**A holiday rental.**
**Tilde Stand:** the same Wi-Fi, standing up on a counter.

items: **NFC sticker:** 1 round sticker, 25 mm: an NTAG216 holds a full contact card; an NTAG215 is fine for a link or your guest Wi-Fi. Search “NTAG216 25mm round NFC sticker”.
